frames.title: Build a clear dramatic spine
frames.summary: Setup, confrontation, and resolution should each change the pressure on the protagonist.
principles: Act One defines the normal world, goal, and inciting disruption.
Act Two escalates obstacles, reversals, and costly choices.
Act Three pays off the central question through decisive action.
Major turns should force a new strategy, not just a new location.
patterns: Use an act break when the protagonist crosses a point of no return.
Track rising stakes across internal, interpersonal, and external lines.
antiPatterns: Do not let the middle become repetitive problem solving.
Do not resolve the climax with information that was withheld from the audience.

frames.title: Escalate through linked movements
frames.summary: Five acts create finer escalation and recovery beats than a broad three-act sweep.
principles: Separate exposition, complication, crisis, climax, and aftermath into distinct dramatic movements.
Let each act end on a sharper complication than the last.
Use the fourth act to compress inevitability before the climax.
Reserve the final act for consequence, not new premise-building.
patterns: Use act outs to force audience anticipation into the next movement.
Pair each act with a specific tactical objective.
antiPatterns: Do not split acts so finely that scenes feel arbitrary.
Do not repeat the same emotional beat at multiple act endings.

frames.title: Use stages to externalize transformation
frames.summary: Mythic structure works best when each stage pressures identity, not just plot logistics.
principles: The call should reveal what the hero lacks or resists.
Mentors and thresholds should change capability or worldview.
The ordeal must cost the old self something real.
The return matters only if the hero brings back usable change.
patterns: Mirror an early fear with a late empowered choice.
Use allies and tests to make growth visible scene by scene.
antiPatterns: Do not force every named stage if the story loses momentum.
Do not confuse spectacle with inner transformation.

frames.title: Keep the audience oriented through beats
frames.summary: A beat sheet helps maintain momentum, tonal promise, and commercial readability.
principles: Open with an image that frames the starting condition.
State the thematic argument early enough to track later payoffs.
Use the midpoint to reframe the promise or danger of the premise.
Drive the finale with an earned synthesis of character and plot.
patterns: Give the protagonist an early empathy beat before asking for audience patience.
Use beat naming as a planning tool, not a performance requirement.
antiPatterns: Do not treat timing targets as more important than scene truth.
Do not let familiar beat labels flatten originality.

frames.title: Create momentum through contrast and reveal
frames.summary: This structure builds interest by juxtaposition and perspective shift rather than direct conflict alone.
principles: Introduce the situation cleanly before complicating it.
Develop familiarity so the turn lands as meaningful contrast.
Let the twist reveal a new relationship, not random novelty.
Resolve by integrating the contrast into a richer understanding.
patterns: Use the third movement to show the same material from a surprising angle.
Favor thematic resonance over adversarial escalation.
antiPatterns: Do not mistake a twist for a disconnected gimmick.
Do not strip away all tension; curiosity still needs shape.

frames.title: Center action on need-driven change
frames.summary: The circle keeps plot attached to a character leaving comfort, adapting, and returning altered.
principles: Start by defining what feels normal for the character.
Move the character toward a want that exposes a deeper need.
Make adaptation costly enough to produce visible growth.
The return should show what has been gained and what cannot be regained.
patterns: Use each circle step to test a different survival strategy.
Keep the emotional logic simple enough to pitch in one sentence.
antiPatterns: Do not confuse motion with transformation.
Do not let the return simply reset the status quo.

frames.title: Favor emotional clarity and causality
frames.summary: Audience engagement grows when events connect through desire, choice, and surprise that still feels inevitable.
principles: Build around what the audience cares about, not what the writer knows.
Keep cause and effect legible even in imaginative worlds.
Let coincidence create problems more often than solutions.
Simplify until the heart of the scene becomes unavoidable.
patterns: Pitch the story as 'once upon a time... until finally...' to test flow.
Use honesty in character reaction before adding cleverness.
antiPatterns: Do not protect favorite ideas that stop the story moving.
Do not make exposition carry emotional work by itself.
